builtin_sounds.doc: two voices resolving to a chord
builtin_sounds.name: builtin:harmony

commands.long:
Read and change jingle's settings. Changes are validated and take effect immediately.

Keys:
  enabled          true|false  master switch
  cooldown         <seconds>   quiet time after a sound, per event, so a
                               burst of commits plays once (default 3, 0 off)
  volume           0-100       playback volume (default 100); needs afplay,
                               pw-play, paplay, or ffplay (not aplay or
                               JINGLE_PLAYER)
  commit.enabled   true|false  play on git commit
  commit.sounds    <file>...   sounds for commits; one is picked at random
  push.enabled     true|false  play on git push
  push.sounds      <file>...   sounds for pushes; one is picked at random
  push.when        success|attempt
                               success (default): play once the push went
                               through; attempt: play when pre-push passes
  merge.enabled    true|false  play when a merge makes a merge commit (default
                               off; fast-forwards and squashes stay quiet)
  merge.sounds     <file>...   sounds for merges; one is picked at random

Booleans also accept on/off. Sound files (mp3 wav aiff aif m4a ogg flac) are
copied into jingle's data dir, so moving the original later is fine.

Built-in sounds need no file; use them by name in any sounds list:
  builtin:chime    two-note rising bell (commit default)
  builtin:fanfare  quick rising brass arpeggio (push default)
  builtin:harmony  two voices resolving to a chord (merge default)
  builtin:boom     snare hit into an 808 drop

"config set <event>.sounds" replaces the whole list ("" clears it);
"config add" and "config remove" change one entry at a time.

push.when success needs git 2.28+. With older git, and for pushes to a URL
rather than a named remote (no remote-tracking ref moves), push plays on
attempt. A merge that stops on a conflict plays the commit sound when you
commit the resolution.

Add one or more sound files to an event's list. Each sound is copied
into jingle's data dir; on every commit or push one sound from the list is
picked at random. Adding a sound that is already in the list reports
changed=false.
commands.short: Add sounds to an event's list

flags.name: repo
flags.usage: repo to check (default: the current directory, if it is a repo)

commands.long:
Check the install, config, sound files, audio player, git version, and
the repo in the current directory (or --repo), and report each problem with
a severity and a fix. The report has the same fields as "jingle status",
plus "repo" when a repo was checked.

Problems with severity "error" stop sounds; "warning" means sounds play but
not as configured (e.g. push plays on attempt rather than on success).

The repo check catches a repo-level core.hooksPath (husky and similar tools
set one), which overrides jingle's global hooks in that repo. Outside a repo
it is skipped, unless --repo is given.

Exit codes: 0 when there are no errors (warnings allowed); 1 when at least
one error was found (code "problems_found"; the report is still printed on
stdout), or --repo is not a git repository (code "not_a_repo").
commands.short: Find everything that would keep jingle silent, with fixes

flags.name: dry-run
flags.usage: print what would change without changing anything

commands.long:
Install jingle's git hooks globally by pointing the global core.hooksPath
at jingle's hooks dir. Works in every repo with no per-repo setup.

Your existing hooks keep running: each jingle hook first runs the hook git
would have run without jingle (the repo's .git/hooks, or your previous global
core.hooksPath), with the same args, stdin, and exit status. The previous
core.hooksPath is saved so "jingle uninstall" can restore it exactly.

Repos that set their own core.hooksPath (husky and similar) override the
global one, so jingle does not play in them; "jingle doctor" run inside a
repo reports this.

Requires --yes (or --dry-run to preview). Safe to re-run: reports "unchanged".
commands.short: Turn on jingle for every repo (sets global core.hooksPath)

flags.name: sound
flags.usage: play this one of the event's sounds instead of a random one

commands.long:
Play the sound configured for an event, without committing or pushing.
Plays even if the event (or jingle) is turned off, and ignores the
cooldown; the result reports "enabled" so you can tell whether it would
play on a real commit or push.

By default the player starts in the background, as it does from a git hook.
Use --wait to block until playback ends and see player errors.

An event with several sounds plays one at random; --sound picks one (by
its entry, original file, or file name, as "config remove" matches them).
commands.short: Play an event's sound now, to test setup

commands.long:
Play a built-in sound or an audio file at the configured volume,
without adding it to an event. Nothing is changed: no config, no cooldown.
Use "play" to hear the sounds an event already has.

By default the player starts in the background. Use --wait to block until
playback ends and see player errors.
commands.short: Play any sound, to audition it before adding it

commands.long:
Print a machine-readable description of jingle: every command with its
usage, flags, and examples; the config keys with their types, defaults, and
allowed values; the built-in sounds; and the exit, error, and problem codes.
The output is always JSON (--json changes nothing). Its fields are part of
the JSON contract, versioned by schema_version.
commands.short: Describe every command, flag, config key, and code as JSON

commands.long:
Print jingle's agent skill: step-by-step instructions an AI coding agent
follows to install, configure, check, and remove jingle. It is a Claude Code
skill (SKILL.md with frontmatter), and plain markdown for any other agent. It
matches this jingle version.

Claude Code users can also install it from the plugin marketplace:
  /plugin marketplace add OPDhaker/jingle
  /plugin install jingle@jingle
commands.short: Print setup instructions for AI agents (a Claude Code skill)

commands.long:
Report everything needed to decide what to do next: whether jingle is
installed, the global/system/previous core.hooksPath, the effective config,
the detected audio player, the git version, and any problems (each with a
severity and a fix). Always exits 0 when it can report; check "problems" for
issues, or use "jingle doctor", which also checks the current repo and exits
1 when something needs fixing.
commands.short: Show install state, settings, player, and problems

flags.name: dry-run
flags.usage: print what would change without changing anything

flags.name: purge
flags.usage: also delete jingle's config and imported sounds

commands.long:
Remove jingle's global hooks and restore the global core.hooksPath that was
set before "jingle install" (or unset it if there was none). If install
created the [core] section or the global gitconfig file, those are removed
too, so the file ends up byte-for-byte as before.

If something else changed core.hooksPath after install, it is left alone.
Your config and imported sounds are kept, so a later install picks them up.
With --purge they are deleted too, along with jingle's config and data dirs
(a dir is kept if it holds files jingle did not create). The jingle binary
itself is not removed; delete it with your package manager or rm.

Requires --yes (or --dry-run to preview). Safe to re-run: reports "unchanged".
commands.short: Turn off jingle everywhere and restore your git config

env.name: JINGLE_HOME

error_codes.meaning: Unknown command or flag, wrong number of arguments.
`config` with an unknown key, or `add`/`remove` on a key that isn't a sound list.

`config set` with a value of the wrong type or out of range, an audio file of an unsupported type, or an unknown `builtin:` sound (also for `preview`); `config remove` of a sound that isn't in the list.
`doctor --repo <dir>` where the dir isn't in a git repository.
git is not installed or not on PATH.
`doctor`: a git command failed unexpectedly while checking the repo.
`install` could not finish (git config or file write failed). Safe to retry.
`uninstall` could not finish. Safe to retry.
The config file can't be parsed.
`config set/add` with a file that doesn't exist, `play --sound` naming a sound that isn't in the event's list, or `preview` of a file that doesn't exist.
`play` for an event with no sounds set.
`play`: every sound file for the event is gone.
No audio player found, or `JINGLE_PLAYER` isn't executable.
The player could not be started (or, with `play --wait`, exited non-zero).
The config or data dir can't be determined (no home dir).
`doctor` found at least one `error` problem. The report is still on stdout.

exit_codes.meaning: The requested state was reached, including "unchanged" (already that way).
Error: the requested state was not reached. For `doctor`: at least one problem has severity `error`.
Usage: bad command, flag, or argument, or `--yes` missing on `install`/`uninstall`.

problem_codes.meaning: Something changed the global `core.hooksPath` after install.
This repo sets its own `core.hooksPath` (husky and similar), so jingle doesn't run here.
Installed hooks are from another jingle version.
The binary the hooks call is gone, but `jingle` is on PATH.
The binary the hooks call is gone and `jingle` isn't on PATH.
The config file can't be parsed.
An enabled event has no sounds.
Every sound file for an event is gone, or names an unknown built-in (error), or only some of them are (warning).
No audio player found, or `JINGLE_PLAYER` is bad.
`volume` < 100 but the player can't change the volume.
git < 2.28: push plays on attempt, not on success.
